chapter: Leading the band after Chick Webb, 1939-40
title: A week at Loew's State and unkind reviews
summary: The band played Loew's State; critics said Beeson looked like the ghost of Chick Webb.

bands.name: Ella Fitzgerald and Her Famous Orchestra

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit

blocks.x: And I think before we left to go on this long tour, we got a date. I think we played Loew's State.
We did play one week at Loew's State Theater.
Which one was this? Where was this one located?
On Broadway. The big theater on Loew's State. (Inaudible) they changed the name -- got another theater there now. Big Loew's State Theater -- right up the street from the Paramount.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Used to be the Paramount. Right across the street was the big Loew's State Theater. That was a theater that had all the big shows. And we played one week there.
What the critics did to us was a very bad thing. Some papers wrote up the band -- the show and everything -- the show was great and everything. And Ella was great and --
Okay. The critics said that Bill Beeson looked like the ghost of Chick Webb.
But anyway, we're on our way -- we're going out of town. We left to go on this tour. The first stop I think was Pittsburg.
